newsitem.title: USA: Converse hits counterfeiters in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Converse hits counterfeiters in Mexico.

text.p: Converse Inc said raids to uncover the illegal manufacture of counterfeit athletic footwear were conducted at warehouses and plants belonging Maytek SA de CV in Mexico.

During the raid, conducted at the beginning of Maytek's production run of counterfeit shoes, hundreds of pairs of counterfeit canvas All Star sneakers were found on Maytek's assembly lines in San Francisco del Rincon, in the state of Guanajato, Converse said.
Converse has been investigating Maytek for over a year, and has been working closely with the Mexican Institute of Industrial Copyrighting (IMPI), said Converse general counsel Jack Green.
"Converse continues to take an aggressive stand against any and all counterfeit activity associated with its products in order to protect the company's extremely valuable trademarks," Green said.

In March, about 250,000 pairs of counterfeit canvas All Star sneakers, manufactured in China and bound for distribution in California and Mexico, were seized from American Shoe Corp in Los Angeles, Converse said. Those shoes were worth about $250,000.
Maytek manufactures its own line of Mayco brand footwear, said outside legal counsel Harley Lewin.

Local newspaper AM in San Francisco del Rincon said on Wednesday that a firm called Mayco International faced a fine of up to 6,000 pesos ($750) from the IMPI. San Francisco del Rincon has a population of about 40,000 and is 200 miles northwest of Mexico City.

AM said Mayco director Luis Miguel Camarena confirmed an "inspection visit" by IMPI had taken place about two weeks previously, which had uncovered "similarities between products made...and Converse sports shoes."
"I shall take more care in future over manufacturing my brands to avoid future legal problems with Converse or any other international brand," AM quoted Camarena as saying.
IMPI officials in Mexico City were unavailable for comment.
Last year, another shoemaking firm in San Francisco del Rincon, Concord, had hundreds of pairs of sports shoes confiscated for presumed counterfeiting of the Nike brand, AM added.
